knowledgeText:
Some guidelines to keep in mind when working on / closing Cases. 
We got some negative surveys that could probably have been (partially) prevented by the following actions. 
 
Short list (in no particular order of importance): 
1) Keep an eye on responsiveness. 
2) Inform customers of APAR (Closure) Notifications 
3) Open Documentation defects 
4) Soft Closures (close with a call) 
5) Make meaningful first contact.  
6) Be clear in your communication 
7) Proper tagging of duplicate or non-surveyable cases 
8) Make sure that your Cases have a Problem Statement as a Subject 
9) Revisit the Business Impact and Deadlines once in a while. 
 
 
Longer version: 
1) Keep an eye on responsiveness 
We all are busy, but do try to get to Cases where customers have replied in a timely manner. 
Also, if you are waiting for L3 to respond, do not do this silently. When you ask L3 for an update / feedback, also make a customer visible post that you are further discussing the issue with L3. This way, even when the customer does not get an answer / solution, they at least know that something is still happening. 
If L3 is not responding, bring it up in an L2L3 call, or reach out to a team lead or a manager, so that we can contact the L3 manager to get some movement. 
 
 
2) Inform customers of APAR (Closure) Notifications 
When providing an APAR to a customer: 
a. Tell them to subscribe to the APAR to get notified of changes in it's Status, as well as fix notifications. 
We have had complaints from a customer that they 'had to find out themselves' that the APAR was fixed. 
b. Tell them to enable / configure the My IBM Notifications. 
Sometimes we also provide APAR document link for APARs that are still in the process of being published. Then tell the customer to enable Notifications in their My IBM, so that they get informed of new APAR documents, including their own. 
https://www.ibm.com/systems/support/myview/subscription/css.wss/ 
 
 
3) Open Documentation defects: 
If you encounter documentation defects, APARs that are incorrectly in the OPEN state, APARs that are not documented in the Fix List (that are not PSIRT APARs), etc, take action. 
Open a Doc defect in Jira, Bring the open APAR up in the L2L3 meetings. 
 
 
4) Soft Closures (close with a call) 
Especially if the customer seems unhappy about something. 
As Pooja mentioned, be sure to check to see if you addressed all of the customer's questions or concerns before closing a Case. 
If necessary open a new Case for new open questions or concerns. 
Having a correct Problem statement as the Case subject (As soon as possible, not as part of the closure of the Case) will help to clarify why a new Case is needed. 
 
 
5) Make meaningful first contact.  
Don't just inform customers that you will be working on the Case. At least perform a basic Situation Appraisal. 
Check with them if you understand their problem description correctly. Ask them for the business impact and the deadlines, if both are not clearly defined in the Case description or Business Impact fields. 
 
 
6) Be clear in your communication 
Try to be clear in the answers you provide. Provide examples where useful / needed. 
Ask the customer to confirm that they understand the solution. 
If you get a solution from L3 that you do not understand, ask them to explain it to you, so that you can explain it to the customer. 
 
 
7) Proper tagging of duplicate or non-surveyable cases 
When you have a Case that you close as a duplicate (that may be closed without any work being done), be sure to fill out the correct fields during closure. Duplicate Cases are exempt from surveys. But it may not be abused to evade surveys. Duplicate Case closures are visible to managers. 
https://merlin-playbook.mybluemix.net/#/documents/b26c440b95ba6a02d6950bc8d3ad7da4 
If you are not sure if any of the survey exemption options apply to your Case, check with a team lead or a manager. 
Survey exemptions should be rare, not common. 



 
8) Make sure that your Cases have a Problem Statement as a Subject 
This makes sure that: 
1) it is clear to you and the customer which exact problem/concern this Case is about 
2) you can split off new questions in to new Cases 
3) other people can more easily understand what the Case is about 
And don't be afraid to change / update the Subject of the Case as our understanding of the issue / concern gets more clear during the investigation. 
 
 
9) Revisit the Business Impact and Deadlines once in a while. 
Business impact and deadlines are thigs that change over time. 
Something that starts as a Sev4 can become a Sev2 when it takes a long time to resolve, because deadlines creep up or get introduced. 
Don't be afraid to check with the customer if they have changed over time. Customers do not always volunteer this information, and that is when it becomes a 'We need to fix this by next week Sev1)

knowledgeText:
Objective: 
This document provides standardized processes for assigning backups and Case workload handling during the time a TSE is away on vacation or leave.  
  
Process Models: 
The process considers three major scenarios of short vacations, Long vacations and leaves: 
  
Backup Process for short vacations: 
Short vacations are referred to anytime a TSE is going to be away/off for at least 1 and up to 3 consecutive business days. The TSE/QMON is responsible to ensure the following tasks are done before taking their short vacation: 
TSE: If time permits, start to alert customers to your time out of office so they are aware. 
TSE: Distinguish the active Cases (Cases which require immediate or proactive attention) from the Passive Cases. 
TSE: Make sure active cases are clear on next steps. 
TSE: Provide a list of active Cases to the team.   
QMON to assign active Cases. Add assignees name to the Keyword field.   
QMON: Add the TSEs name to the Backup column in the QMON view.  If customer replies to an unexpected Case, QMON will assign the case to the next available TSE by putting their name in the Keyword field. 
TSE: Send an email to inform the team about: their return date. 
 
   Note 1: Backup TSE should either add a View or Pipeline to find cases where they are assigned to the Keyword field. 
Note 2: It is not required to change owner or resolver of a PMR for short vacations to the backup TSE. The original Case owner will take all their Cases back upon their return. 
     
Backup Process for Long vacations/Leave: 
Long vacations/Leave are referred to anytime a TSE is going to be away/off longer than 4 consecutive business days. The TSE is responsible to ensure the following tasks are done before taking their long vacation: 
  
TSE: If time permits, start to alert customers to your time out of office so they are aware. 
QMON: Withhold assigning new cases to TSE 1 day prior to the TSE's leave (*under normal Case load) to focus on closing and minimizing the workload that will be transferred to backup TSEs. 
TSE: Distinguish the active Cases (Cases which require immediate or proactive attention) from the Passive Cases. 
TSE: Make sure active cases are clear on next steps. 
TSE: Provide a list of active Cases to the team.   
QMON to assign active Cases. Add assignees name to the Keyword field.  
QMON: Add the TSEs name to the Backup column in the QMON view.  If customer replies to an unexpected Case, QMON will assign the case to the next available TSE by putting their name in the Keyword field. 
TSE: Send an email to inform the team about: their return date. 
 
   Note 1: Backup TSE should either add a View or Pipeline to find cases where they are assigned to the Keyword field. 
Note 2: It is not required to change owner or resolver of a Case for long vacations to the  backup TSE. The TSE should decide based on the effort of the Case so far if it is appropriate to take ownership or not.   
*Normal load is referred to anytime when the team is not overloaded and no TSE has more than a maximum of 3 Cases per day. 
Exceptions and agreed upon changes: 
  
It is important to note that the above processes are defined for normal conditions and its details can be overwritten if all the involved parties are in agreement to the change. Here are some examples of such exceptions or edge cases: 
  
TSE X is a focal for Client A. TSE Y is going on a short vacation and has only 3 Active Cases from Client A. TSE X agrees, TSE X can be the backup for all 3 Cases. 
TSE X is leaving on a 1 week long vacation starting a Monday and TSE Y is leaving on a 2 week vacation starting the Thursday of the same week. Although it is best to spread the workload, it would be a better practice to not assign TSE Y as a backup to avoid having the Case change multiple hands.

RedHat Marketplace (RHM) Case Handling
Wednesday, August 19, 2020
8:22 AM
 
Highlights:
 
For RHM cases, use the email feature from Feed v2 to contact the customer. Customers can't see posts.
Include the customer in the CC field.  REMOVE your email id from the BCC field
Do not change the Subject of the email.  The values in the Subject trigger an update in the RHM SN case.
Do NOT remove the keyword RHMSUPPORT from the parent case
When case is complete, close the parent case as normal.  The SN team will get notified and close things out on their side
 
 
Details:
 
RHM uses an IBM instance of ServiceNow (nothing related to our HCL instance).
 
To engage another IBM product for help, RHM will use the email-to-case SF feature from their SN instance to open a SF case against their SF mission, Open Marketplace.  To see an example case in the SF staging environment, search for case TS003210841. 
 
The RH team will then:
  1) Open a skills case for their team.  They want to continue to monitor the case.
  2) Add the keyword RHMSUPPORT to the parent case.
  3) Change the primary case to us.
  
The SwivelToSf_EngageWithIbmSupport.docx document is written for the RHM agent, not us.  It just shows the process the RHM side goes through to engage an IBM team.
 
<<SwivelToSf_EngageWithIbmSupport.docx>>
Here is the note from the RHM team with how things will be different when working with a RHM primary case:
 
Hello UCD Team,
 
In working with some of the other IBM product teams, it was determined that the most simple way for Red Hat Marketplace to engage with internal IBM teams is for RHM to send a primary to your team and keep the secondary.
 
Things to note  for RHM that are different from working with "normal" IBM product teams:
Cases for RHM in Salesforce are of type "Email to Case" 
Public post does not send an update to the client
Use email functionality within the Salesforce Case (top of each case) to engage with customer 
Keep rhmspte2c@us.ibm.com on CC as this will auto populate our ServiceNow support ticketing system
Don't forget to keep the customer on CC as this will keep everyone in the loop
RHM Support will use the Salesforce keyword "RHMSUPPORT" to trigger certain Salesforce events which will alert our team on any case updates.  Please do not remove this keyword.
Prior to sending primary to your team, RHM will change the case contact information to the customer contact.  This "should" trigger automatic re-entitlement so the case should arrive to your team as entitled.  Regardless if case auto-re-entitles, all of the entitlement information we have pertaining to the customer will be contained in the case text as we had previously discussed.
 
Please see the attachment.  It is the segment of education I have provided to my team in discussing how we will engage with other IBM product teams.
 
Please let me know if you have any questions.
 
Information about how to work a E2C case using the built in email functionality is here:  https://merlin-playbook.mybluemix.net/#/documents/b26c440b95ba6a02d6950bc8d3ad3d01
Direct link to the 1 min 30 sec video is here:  https://learn.ibm.com/mod/page/view.php?id=29058
Info about the E2C feature overview is here: https://merlin-playbook.mybluemix.net/#/documents/826413624d29ac02332c046fe682f296
 
Playbook link that describes the HM workflow:  https://merlin-playbook.mybluemix.net/#/documents/ae12ec4a8bb73d95a016bbddb24a4aa4
 
Follow on question:  1) What about attachements?  2) What about HIPPA?
 
From the RHM team:
 
1.  Attachments will come to your team via Ecurep.  The RHM support portal does not yet have the ability to upload attachments.  But we are working closely with the Ecurep team to integrate this functionality into ServiceNow.  Our interim work-around is for us to have the customer upload the docs to the Salesforce case that we need to create to engage your team anyway.  Therefore, aside from the customer having to go to a different site to upload data (https://www.secure.ecurep.ibm.com/app/upload_sf), the data would be found in the location they expect.  As an aside, if additional data was needed, the customer could go to https://www.secure.ecurep.ibm.com/app/upload_sf with the Salesforce number OR if the agent sends a request via Ecurep email, the customer could always attach a file to the Ecurep email response back.
 
2.  We are not (knowingly) handling HIPAA customers at this time.  But when we do, I aim to use Blue Diamond as our solution unless something better comes along before.

knowledgeText:
Objective: 
This document provides standardized processes for assigning backups and PMR workload handling during the time a TSE is away on vacation or leave.  
  
Process Models: 
The process considers three major scenarios of short vacations, Long vacations and leaves: 
  
Backup Process for short vacations: 
Short vacations are referred to anytime a TSE is going to be away/off for at least 1 and up to 3 consecutive business days. The TSE is responsible to ensure the following tasks are done before taking their short vacation: 
Minimize the work required during their absence by negotiating commitment dates that are after his/her return with the customers. i.e. ask customers if the PMR work can wait till the TSEâ€™s return  
Determine and distinguish the active PMRs (PMRs which require immediate or proactive attention) from the Passive PMRs. 
Find a general and specific (if needed) backup TSE(s) to handle their PMRs while s/he is away and inform clients of the designated backup(s): 
General backup: a TSE who act as a backup for passive PMRs 
Specific backup: a TSE who takes the responsibility of handling an active PMR(s) 
  
    Note 1: It is important to not assign the same TSE as both general and specific backup point and spread the workload as much as possible among the team members. 
  
Note 2: It is not required to change owner or resolver of a PMR for short vacations to the general or specific backup individual. The original PMR owner will take all their PMRs back upon their return. 
  
4.  Send an email to inform the team about: their return date, the general and specific backup TSEs along with the PMR number,action taken and action plan(s) of the active PMRs. 
    
Backup Process for Long vacations/Leave: 
Long vacations/Leave are referred to anytime a TSE is going to be away/off longer than 4 consecutive business days. The TSE is responsible to ensure the following tasks are done before taking their long vacation: 
  
Minimize the work required during their absence by negotiating commitment dates that are after their return date with their customers. i.e. ask customers if the PMR work can wait till the TSEâ€™s return  
The TSE should withhold from taking any new PMRs 1 day prior to their leave (under normal PMR load*), to focus on closing and minimizing the workload that will be transferred to backup individual(s). 
determine and distinguish the active PMRs (PMRs which require immediate or proactive attention) from the Passive PMRs. 
Find a general and specific (if needed) backup TSE(s) to handle their PMRs while they are away: 
General backup: a TSE who act as a backup for passive PMRs 
Specific backup: a TSE who takes the responsibility of handling an active PMR(s) 
  
    Note 1: It is important to not assign the same TSE as both general and specific backup point and spread the workload as much as possible among the team members. 
  
Note 2: It is required to change the resolver of an active PMR to the specific backup individual. The PMR should go back to original owner of the PMR once the original owner returns. 
  
     5.   Send an email to inform the team about: their return date, the general and specific backup TSEs along with the PMR number,action taken and action plan(s) of the active PMRs. 
   
*Normal load is referred to anytime when the team is not overloaded and no TSE has more than a maximum of 3 PMRs per day. 
Exceptions and agreed upon changes: 
  
It is important to note that the above processes are defined for normal conditions and its details can be overwritten if all the involved parties are in agreement to the change. Here are some examples of such exceptions or edge cases: 
  
TSE X is a focal for Client A. TSE Y is going on a short vacation and has only 3 Active PMRs from Client A. According to Note 1 under short vacation process the workload must be spread among the team. Now if TSE X and TSE Y are in agreement, TSE X can be the backup for all 3 PMRs. 
Consider the above case again, when TSE X also agrees to be the general backup for a plausible reason. 
TSE X is leaving on a 1 week long vacation starting a Monday and TSE Y is leaving on a 2 week vacation starting the Thursday of the same week. Although it is best to spread the workload, it would be a better practice to not assign TSE Y as a backup to avoid having the PMR change multiple hands.  
etc. 
General and Specific Backup Process: 
  
A General backup should perform the following tasks: 
Use ICSWâ€™s combined Queue feature to add the away TSEâ€™s working queue to his main view and monitor their working queue incase a PMR is waken up or is back from the FUP state. 
Monitor the inbound queue for any update on all of of the away TSEâ€™s PMRs except the ones that have specific backups. 
Note 1: The General backup does not necessarily have to take and work of all the PMRs that are waken up. Having said that, s/he is responsible for all such PMRs and must ensure to distribute the work among the team members through direct verbal/chat/email agreement with specific members. 
  
A Specific backup should perform the following tasks: 
Understand the business impact and urgency of the assigned PMR(s) and prioritize the assigned PMR(s) accordingly. The backup work should not be treated as second priority to the Backup personâ€™s own PMRs.  
Monitor the inbound queue for any updates on the PMR. 
Clean Queue Policy: 
It is vital to keep the inbound queue clean at all time. This not only allows for the backup points to spot PMRs with actions pending but also allows team members to coordinate their work better. i.e. TSEâ€™s can identify and inform each other of PMRs going on alarm to save responsiveness points for the team.  
  
Here are some recommended practices that will help keeping a clean queue: 
  
  
If the primary of a PMR is on the front queue remove all the secondaries that are accompanying it. 
Ensure there are no PMRs (secondary/Primary) left on the queue from last day(s) 
If you are on a long call/meeting and the your PMRs are piling up on the front queue, requeue the PMR you are currently dispatched to, clean you PMRs by moving them to your working queue, redispatch to the initial PMR and correct PSAR metric. 
At the end of each day transfer all of your PMRs from front queue to your working queue.

Blue Diamond Shared Network File System
Overview
The Blue Diamond shared network file system can be accessed only by IBM Employees from:
A Citrix Standard Blue Diamond Desktop - click on the Standard (H Drive) icon.
Most PMR systems
Windows - the Blue Diamond shared network file system is mapped to the H:\ Drive
Linux and AIX - the Blue Diamond shared network file system is mounted as /standard.
Shared Network Files System Directories
Several directories will be displayed when you first access the shared network file system.
General Access folders that IBMers can use:
callhome - Contains auto-generated files from HW PMRs.
inprodrep - Contains copies of non-client files (ex. tools, applications, scripts etc.) uploaded to the inprodrep FTP folder. 45 day clean up policy.
pmr and sf - Are described in the Accessing client files on the Standard Blue Diamond shared network file system section.
Restricted Access folders:
bdadmin -  Only accessible by Blue Diamond system administrators.
cesroot -  GPFS folder. Restricted to all users.
teams - Private folders reserved for individual teams.
uscs - Contains files uploaded by NASA & Blue Origin.
Accessing Client Files on the Standard Blue Diamond Shared Network File System.
Establish a Citrix connection to Blue Diamond
Login to a PMR analysis system PMR analysis system
Access the shared network file system using the method pertaining to the PMR analysis system OS below
For Cognitive Support Platform cases, the folder naming convention follows the pattern â€œ/standard/sf/tsxxx/xxx/tsxxxxxxxxxâ€ where the sub-folders are created based on the first two-three digit segments of the case. For example:
 
Windows:
Case # TS123456789: H:\sf\ts123\456\ts123456789
Case # TS000123456: H:\sf\ts000\123\ts000123456
Linux/AIX:
Case # TS123456789: /standard/sf/ts123/456/ts123456789
Case # TS000123456: /standard/sf/ts000/123/ts000123456
Other platforms currently do not have access to the shared network file system.
For PMRs, the folder naming convention follows the pattern â€œ/standard/pmr/F/S/PMRâ€ where F and S are the first and second digits of the problem number and the PMR is the full comma separated PMR number.  For example: 
 
â€‹Windows:
PMR # 12345,ABC,000: H:\pmr\1\2\12345,ABC,000\
PMR # 82201,442,000: H:\pmr\8\2\82201,442,000\â€‹
Linux/AIX:
PMR # 12345,ABC,000: /standard/pmr/1/2/12345,ABC,000/
PMR # 82201,442,000: /standard/pmr/8/2/82201,442,000/
 Other platforms currently do not have access to the shared network file system.
All files stored on the shared network file system that include the case/PMR number in the file name or the name of the associated directory will be deleted automatically when the case/PMR is Closed and Archived.
NOTE: If the shared network file system is not available, you can still download the files from the secure FTP server.  See How To Download Client Files To a PMR System From the Blue Diamond Secure FTP Site
Mapping the Shared Network File System on Windows
H: on all Windows PMR analysis systems will be auto-mounted. Follow the steps below if auto-mount is not working.
The following shows how to map the shared network file system to access client files.
1. Use Remote Desktop Connection to access a Windows host, then:
Click on "File Explorer folder"
Right click "Network"
Click "Map network drive"
2. Provide the following information:
Select a Drive letter.  H is commonly used.  If H is already in use on this host, select another letter
Enter the Folder name as shown in the screen shot below. In addition to 10.0.4.87, you can also use: 10.0.4.77, 10.0.4.78, 10.0.4.80, 10.0.4.85, 10.0.4.86, 10.0.4.88 or 10.0.4.89
Do not click "Browse"
Check the box "Reconnect at logon". If you don't, you will need to map the drive each time you log in
Click "Finish"
After it is mounted, you will see something similar to the following. You can now access directories on the shared network file system. 

Modifying Client Data
Client data shared on the shared network file system is accessible to all users.  Please be aware, if you modify client data, this will impact any other users of the same data. If needed, first make a copy in a sub-folder under the PMR/Case folder.
